:::{#thm-pois-fitted-totals}
#### Poisson regression reproduces observed totals

Suppose we fit the Poisson regression model (@def-poisson-reg)
with linear predictor $\eta(\vx) = \b_0 + \b_1 x_1 + \dots + \b_p x_p$
to independent observations $(y_i, \vx_i, t_i)$, $i = 1, \lds, n$,
and that the [maximum likelihood estimate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-mle) $\evb$ exists.
Write $x_{i0} \eqdef 1$ for the intercept's covariate,
and $\emu_i \eqdef t_i \expf{\eta(\vx_i)}$ evaluated at $\vb = \evb$
for the fitted mean of observation $i$.
Then, for every $j \in \cb{0, 1, \lds, p}$:

$$
\sumin x_{ij} \, y_i = \sumin x_{ij} \, \emu_i
$$ {#eq-pois-fitted-totals}

In particular,
taking $j = 0$,
the fitted event counts add up to the observed event count:
$\sumin y_i = \sumin \emu_i$.
If $x_j$ is the [indicator variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/data.html#def-indicator-variable) for a group,
then the fitted event counts in that group add up to the group's observed event count.
:::
